key_insight: Replace the inherited box-driven paradigm with a keypoint-driven representation learning scheme so single-stage, YOLO-like detectors can predict human keypoints more accurately and efficiently in real time.
problem_solved: Single-stage multi-person pose estimators often rely on box-centric modeling from object detection, causing feature misalignment and suboptimal keypoint localization under real-time, multi-scale settings. ER-Pose addresses this gap by explicitly designing representation learning around keypoints rather than bounding boxes.
method: Introduce a keypoint-centric representation module that aligns and aggregates features around predicted keypoint locations instead of relying on box features.
Design an efficient, multi-scale head compatible with YOLO-like backbones that decouples localization (person centers/boxes) from keypoint regression for better accuracy-latency tradeoffs.
Use lightweight training objectives and feature fusion to improve robustness in crowded and scale-varying scenes while keeping inference real-time.
impact: Makes single-stage pose estimators both more accurate and more practical for deployment by improving keypoint localization without sacrificing real-time throughput—useful for video, robotics, AR/VR, and edge applications.

paper_title: ER-Pose: Rethinking Keypoint-Driven Representation Learning for Real-Time Human Pose Estimation
paper_authors: Nanjun Li, Pinqi Cheng, Zean Liu, Minghe Tian, Xuanyin Wang
